title: RTEC Limited English Proficiency language-assistance workflow — January 2026 plan
trigger: A customer, applicant for transit service, passenger or member of the public needs language assistance to access RTEC transportation information or services.
service_channels: Routing Spanish-speaking callers to a bilingual customer-service resource for reservations/questions.
Translation of written correspondence into English and translation of RTEC's response into Spanish.
Spanish availability on the RTEC website.
Vehicle-operator escalation to dispatch/customer service when the operator cannot communicate effectively.
Community outreach communicating that language assistance is available.
staff_training: CSR and Operations staff are trained to recognize when an LEP person needs assistance and to route the person to an appropriate bilingual customer-service resource.
The 2026 plan states this awareness training is included in CSR/Operations orientation and initial on-the-job training.
The plan states regular retraining is provided and discusses possible additional basic-Spanish/video training.
safe_harbor_and_access: The plan states that its four-factor analysis did not identify a language group meeting the five-percent or 1,000-person written-translation threshold on average across the service area.
The plan nevertheless identifies Hispanic/Latino population growth and provides Spanish brochures, telephone options and website information.
The plan distinguishes written-document safe-harbor provisions from the obligation to provide meaningful oral access where oral language services are needed and reasonable.
The plan states that language-assistance tools are provided at no additional cost to the LEP individual.
ongoing_evaluation: Review how LEP needs were addressed.
Reassess the current LEP population in the service area.
Reassess whether translation-service needs have changed.
Assess whether financial resources are sufficient for needed language assistance.
Update the plan as demographics, documents and services change.
privacy_and_data_controls: Do not promote the names of individual bilingual employees into the generalized process model; maintain role/capability coverage instead.
A current bilingual-capability roster, if operationally needed, should be restricted/internal and updated independently of the public plan.
Language-assistance encounter logs should avoid unnecessary sensitive or identifying detail while retaining enough information for service and compliance evaluation.
currentness_risks: The January 2026 plan names individual bilingual staff. Staffing changes can make those names stale even while the plan remains otherwise current.

The plan mentions free web translation tools as possible resources. Operational use should be governed by current privacy/security/quality standards rather than assuming every historical tool reference remains approved.
Public Spanish/translated pages and printed notices should be checked against the current canonical service/contact data to prevent locale/version drift.
automation_candidates: Restricted capability directory for bilingual staff/resources without publishing employee names into general knowledge.
Language-assistance encounter log with aggregate reporting.
Automated locale/document version checks so English and translated public information change together.
Periodic prompt to rerun demographic/four-factor review when new census/service-area data or major service changes occur.
